Theories

All theories

Named ideas stated formally: a claim, propositions graded by the evidence behind them, the primary studies they rest on, and what counts against them.

TheoryCognitive ectothermyRelying on the environment to supply understanding, as an ectotherm relies on outside heat. McLuhan's hot and cool, read as regulation: what a medium hands over before you have predicted it is not learned, and the capacity it replaces goes untrained.6 propositions · 2 strong · 15 referencesTheoryGround blindnessWhat works, or surrounds you, stops being seen while it is there. Only taking it away shows what it was doing, and what removal shows can be the opposite of what it seemed to do.7 propositions · 2 strong · 20 referencesTheorySelf-extinguishing maintenanceA routine that works removes the symptom that cued and rewarded it, so the routine stops, and a cause that never went away brings the problem back.8 propositions · 2 strong · 16 references

Papers

All papers
Paper series7 papers · read in order or dip in

McLuhan said every medium changes the ratio among our senses. Seven papers take that literally.

Six papers test it — from ADHD and typing to drugs and addiction — and the synthesis finds one configuration that media, drugs and illness all re-temper.

01KrasisThe synthesis of the series: one configuration that media, drugs and illness all re-temper.Synthesis12 min02Sensory syncrasisMcLuhan meant his "sense ratios" literally.The senses20 min03HeterocrasisADHD as a different starting balance of the senses.ADHD16 min04TypomoraMcLuhan said electric media would bring back the voice.Voice & typing22 min05ExocrasisThe computing environment, not the screen, is the medium: keyboard, memory, search and network move part of the configuration of the senses and of memory outside the body.Computing16 min06PharmakrasisEach class of drug sets its own balance of the senses — and the evidence for that is better than for any medium.Drugs18 min07NarcocrasisIn dependence, what goes unseen is not the drug but the shifted baseline: the allostatic state is the medium, the drug its content.Addiction28 min

Each paper cites the published literature with numbered references · published 4–5 October 2026

PaperBuilds on the seriesWhy TemperatureMcLuhan never said why media are hot or cool. Read as regulation, hot and cool describe how much a medium supplies, how much it arouses, and whether the receiver predicts before the answer arrives. Working paper.

Writing

EssayArgue one of the author’s ideas
Guess before you lookAn answer that arrives before you have made a guess leaves little behind. The same tool teaches or deskills depending on that order, and the effort it takes to guess first feels like learning less while it is the part that does the learning.22 Nov·7 min·McLuhan & media theorySelf-extinguishing maintenanceSome problems only stay fixed while you keep treating them — a gap between two teeth, toes pressed too tight. The treatment works, the problem vanishes, it looks cured, you stop, and it comes back. This research named the cycle and the mistake behind it.4 Oct·10 min·Habits & maintenanceThe counter-irritant spiralIn 1964 Marshall McLuhan, reading the stress researcher Hans Selye, wrote that relief "usually proves a greater plague than the initial irritant, like a drug habit." Addiction science later measured the same spiral — and what users stop noticing is not the drug, but their own changed baseline.4 Oct·6 min·McLuhan & media theoryUnverified hunches in AI-assisted software workA hunch that feels right gets handed to a collaborator as if it had been checked. When the collaborator is an AI that starts every session blank, nobody checks it at all.9 Oct·9 min·AI-directed developmentSeeing what you rely onA tool, habit or substance in daily use stops being noticed, so it is judged only by what it is like to have it. Experiments that take things away find effects their users could not see, and sometimes the opposite of what having them seemed to do.22 Nov·7 min·McLuhan & media theoryAll 11 essays
BriefAnswer one question from the evidence
Paying yourself to do your own tasksFinancial incentives move behaviour while they run, and losses move people more than equal gains. Paying yourself a wage from your own pocket removes most of what the trials rely on; a subscription you earn back by doing the work is a loss-framed stake, and the research rates it the version most likely to work. Nobody has tested it.10 Oct·7 min·ADHD & attentionCanadian recessions and the mortgage channelEvery major Canadian downturn since 1980 carries a monetary-policy fingerprint, and housing is how the decision reaches people. The clearest case is 1990, where the campaign overshot its own target and Toronto prices did not pass their 1989 peak until 2002.10 Oct·10 min·HousingTemporary foreign workers and Canadian innovationThe research that says immigration drives innovation studies points-selected skilled migration. Canada's intake since 2016 has been mostly temporary and low-wage, and the causal work on cheap labour runs the other way — a 1% rise in low-skill wages lifts automation patenting 2–5%. The Canadian version of that study has never been done.10 Oct·11 min·Canadian economy & policyWhey protein in hot black coffeeCollagen disappears into a hot cup; whey turns it into pale lumps that smell of sulfur. Coffee's acidity sits almost exactly where whey is least stable, and it is served above the temperature that unfolds the protein. The heat-stable ingredients that exist solve it by cutting the protein up, which makes it bitter.10 Oct·10 min·Health & self-careBill C-11 and Canadian creators in 2026Creators were told the Online Streaming Act would cost them their foreign audiences by teaching recommendation systems that Canadian videos go unwatched. Three years after royal assent the regulator has imposed no discoverability requirement on anyone, the money is stayed by a court, and no study has measured the harm.10 Oct·8 min·Canadian mediaAll 26 briefs

Lexicon

Every term

Names for patterns the work found that had none. Each has its own page with a definition, examples and how it differs from existing terms.

TermSING-kruh-sisSensory syncrasisSensory syncrasis is the whole configuration of how a brain combines its senses: how much it trusts each one, how strongly it amplifies all of them, whether it fuses or separates them, the balance between body and world, and how long a setting lasts.In plain words: the balance of the sensesTermnar-KOK-ruh-sisNarcocrasisNarcocrasis is the shifted baseline of drug dependence, with flatter pleasures, a restless body and a raised stress tone, which the person stops perceiving while the drug itself stays vividly noticed.In plain words: the unnoticed baseline of dependenceTermty-poh-MOR-uhTypomoraTypomora is the delay of roughly fifty years in which networked computing stayed typed rather than spoken, because bandwidth, computing power and speech recognition could not yet carry the voice.In plain words: the typed delay
